verdict.rationale: Flagright documents signed webhook events using an `X-Flagright-Signature` header and supports secret rolling with the previous secret kept active, so developers can verify event authenticity. It also documents retries for up to 3 days, but nothing in the evidence shows a unique event ID, idempotency key or other mechanism for deduplicating those retried deliveries. Missing for 10: a documented event ID or idempotency key for deduplicating retried webhooks, signature-verification algorithm details (timestamp or replay tolerance), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can verify alert-event authenticity and deduplicate retried notifications

citations.quote: Flagright signs the webhook events it sends to your endpoints by including a signature in each event's `X-Flagright-Signature` header.
when you roll an endpoint's secret from the Flagright Console, and choose to keep the previous secret active for some period of time
Flagright webhooks have built-in retry methods for 3xx, 4xx, or 5xx response status codes. We will retry for up to 3 days
